Keep old constant names as deprecated module attributes for one release so external imports don't break.
invariants: Do not modify model_map.yaml v2 step entries here — those are owned by E8.

Do not introduce a circuit breaker. The Phase D consensus (gpt-5.2 + claude-opus-4.5 + gpt-5.2-pro) explicitly rejected app-level breakers; per-request failover + --disable-provider kill-switch is the agreed alternative.

Old ladder constants (BALANCED_GROK_OPENROUTER_*, GEMINI_PRIMARY_*, OPTIMAL_*) must remain importable from run_extraction_v5 for one release with a DeprecationWarning emitted on first access. Removal scheduled for the release after E8 lands.
Per-request failover counts toward escalation_max_hops; it does NOT bypass the operator's cap. A ladder of length N can be tried up to N times in a single LLM call before failing.
disabled_providers (--disable-provider CLI) must be honored by per-request failover: a route whose provider is disabled is skipped without attempting the call.
Preserve audit-confirmed fixes F2-CRIT-1 (batch fetch_results) and F2-CRIT-3 (strict batch payload).

pr.title: feat(rte): cell-aliased ladders + per-request failover (E7)
pr.body:
## Summary
- Rewrites 11 hardcoded ladder/route constants in run_extraction_v5.py (L891-987) to derive their routes from `COST_PROFILES[<profile>].cell_aliases` so a model swap requires only an env var or `--model-alias` override, not a code change.
- Adds per-request failover to `_route_ladder_for_phase()` / `call_llm` wrapper: a route returning 5xx / timeout / 429 immediately tries the next route in the ladder before standard backoff retries kick in. Counts toward `escalation_max_hops`.
- Honors `--disable-provider` kill-switch (already wired in cfg by 9085d8a1d): routes whose provider is in the disabled set are skipped during failover.
- Keeps old constant names as importable module attributes with `DeprecationWarning` on access for one release.

## Scope
Limited to run_extraction_v5.py and four new test files. No changes to model_map.yaml v2 (E8 owns that).

## Validation
New tests: failover triggers on 5xx, honors disabled_providers, respects escalation_max_hops, alias resolution works for ladder routes, legacy constants raise DeprecationWarning. Existing cost cap + promptset truth + cost profile tests remain green. Dry-run --print-phase-routing produces valid output with resolved model IDs.

## NOT_RUN
- Live provider calls (RTE_DISABLE_LIVE_LLM_IN_TESTS=1).
- model_map.yaml v3 integration (E8 packet covers).

## Residual Risks / UNKNOWNs
- Per-request failover plus existing retry logic could cumulatively try the same provider many times in one call if multiple ladder rungs share a provider. Cap-honoring needs review.
- DeprecationWarning timing: if any test suite imports run_extraction_v5 with `-W error`, the bare-attribute access in tests will fail. We surface this in a known-issues note.

@codex review

steps.task: Preflight: verify TP-RTE-COSTPROFILE-E4-FINISH-001 is merged (alias resolution is wired into call_llm). Verify worktree clean.
validation: E4-FINISH commits visible in ancestry; otherwise STOP.

steps.task: Catalog every existing ladder constant and every importer. Run grep for `BALANCED_GROK_OPENROUTER_`, `GEMINI_PRIMARY_`, `OPTIMAL_`, `BALANCED_OPENROUTER_` across the repo. Record each importer for the deprecation-warning rollout decision.
validation: Importer inventory captured. Each importer is either updated to read from COST_PROFILES or kept on the deprecated alias path.

steps.task: Design the new ladder-derivation function: `derive_ladder_for_cell(cost_profile, lane_class, capability_tier, stage='primary')` that returns the list of `(provider, model_id, api_key_env)` tuples by reading `COST_PROFILES[cost_profile].cell_aliases` and applying `resolve_cell_alias()` to each placeholder. Wraps with a thin cache keyed on (cost_profile, lane_class, capability_tier, stage, frozenset(cli_alias_overrides), frozenset(disabled_providers)).
validation: Cache key correctly invalidates when CLI overrides or disabled providers change between runs.

steps.task: Replace each ladder constant with a property-like getattr proxy. Module-level `__getattr__(name)` intercepts access to the deprecated names, emits `warnings.warn('Legacy ladder constant {name} is deprecated; use derive_ladder_for_cell()...', DeprecationWarning, stacklevel=2)`, then returns the equivalent ladder derived from COST_PROFILES + the model strings the old constant held. Map the old constants to their canonical (cost_profile, lane_class, capability_tier) cells so the proxy returns the right list.
validation: Each of the 11 old constants resolves to the right cell.

steps.task: Implement per-request failover in `_route_ladder_for_phase()`. The current call_llm caller iterates the ladder via escalation_max_hops; extend so that within a single attempt, on 5xx/timeout/429, the next route is tried immediately (decrementing failover budget, not hop budget). Failover budget = len(ladder) - current_index. Hop budget remains escalation_max_hops.
validation: Logic distinguishes failover (provider error) from escalation (contract failure).

steps.task: Honor cfg.disabled_providers in failover: when iterating the failover candidates, skip any whose `provider` is in cfg.disabled_providers. If all candidates are disabled, raise RuntimeError with a clear message naming the disabled providers.
validation: Skipped routes are logged with reason 'provider_disabled'.
All-disabled case raises with operator-actionable message.

steps.task: Write test_per_request_failover.py (8+ tests): single 500 triggers failover; two consecutive 500s exhaust failover; 200 after failover succeeds; timeout treated like 500; 429 treated like 500; 4xx (non-429) NOT failover (real client error → raise); failover counts against hop budget; ladder of length 1 = no failover possible.

Write test_cell_aliased_ladders.py (6+ tests): derive_ladder_for_cell returns expected list per profile/cell; CLI alias overrides propagate; env vars propagate; cache invalidation on override change; alias cycle raises ValueError; unresolved placeholder returns verbatim.

Write test_disable_provider_kill_switch.py (5+ tests): --disable-provider openai removes openai routes from failover; all-disabled raises; multiple disabled providers honored; case-insensitive matching; invalid provider name logs warning + does not affect resolution.

Write test_legacy_ladder_deprecation_warning.py (4+ tests): access `run_extraction_v5.BALANCED_GROK_OPENROUTER_SYNTHESIS_LADDER` raises DeprecationWarning; warning text names the new derive_ladder_for_cell helper; ladder value still resolves correctly during the deprecation window; warnings.simplefilter('error') makes the access raise as test expects.

Run pal/thinkdeep + pal/challenge on the failover design — specifically: does failover stack with retry backoff dangerously? Could a misconfigured ladder + retry policy cause >100 calls per single LLM request?
validation: Findings either addressed in code or documented as accepted in PROOF.json.

steps.task: Run pal/codereview + pal/precommit. Commit allowlisted files; push; open PR.
validation: PR body includes Summary / Scope / Validation / NOT_RUN / Residual Risks.
